question_text: A bird is flying due North at a speed of $10\text{ m/s}$. A train $250\text{ m}$ long is also travelling due North at a speed of $20\text{ m/s}$. Bird and train are moving in the same vertical plane. How long will the train take to overtake the bird completely?
solution:
Both the bird and the train are moving in the same direction (due North).
Relative velocity of the train with respect to the bird is:
$$v_{\text{rel}} = v_{\text{train}} - v_{\text{bird}} = 20 - 10 = 10\text{ m/s}$$

To overtake the bird completely, the train must cover a distance equal to its length, $L = 250\text{ m}$.
Therefore, time taken is:
$$t = \frac{L}{v_{\text{rel}}} = \frac{250\text{ m}}{10\text{ m/s}} = 25\text{ s}$$

question_text: A stone is dropped into water from a bridge $44.1\text{ m}$ above the water. Time taken by the stone to reach water is
solution:
Initial velocity $u = 0$.
Distance fallen $h = 44.1\text{ m}$.
Acceleration $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$.

Using equation of motion:
$$h = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^2$$
$$44.1 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(9.8)t^2 = 4.9t^2$$
$$t^2 = \frac{44.1}{4.9} = 9 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$

question_text:
For the given acceleration ($a$) versus time ($t$) graph of a body, the body is initially at rest. The velocity ($v$) versus time ($t$) graph will be

[Refer to the given $a\text{--}t$ graph]
diagram_description: Question diagram shows an acceleration-time graph with acceleration decreasing linearly from $a_0$ at $t=0$ to $0$ at time $t$. The options show four velocity-time graphs: (1) straight line with positive slope starting from origin; (2) straight line with negative slope; (3) parabolic curve concave downwards starting from origin with slope decreasing to zero; (4) parabolic curve concave upwards starting from origin.
solution:
From the given $a\text{--}t$ graph, acceleration decreases linearly with time:
$$a(t) = a_0 - k t$$
Since $a = \frac{dv}{dt}$, velocity is obtained by integrating acceleration with initial condition $v(0) = 0$:
$$v(t) = \int_0^t (a_0 - kt)\, dt = a_0 t - \frac{1}{2}kt^2$$

1. At $t = 0$, $v = 0$ and the slope $\frac{dv}{dt} = a_0 > 0$.
2. As $t$ increases, the slope $\frac{dv}{dt} = a(t)$ decreases, reaching zero when $a = 0$.
3. Therefore, the $v\text{--}t$ curve is a parabolic curve concave downwards whose slope continuously decreases to zero, represented by Graph (3).

question_text: A ball is dropped from the roof of a lift. At this moment, the lift is moving downward with an acceleration $a$ ($a < g$). The ratio of acceleration of the ball for an observer inside the lift to the acceleration of ball for an observer on the ground will be
solution:
1. For an observer on the ground (inertial frame), once released, the ball is under the sole influence of gravity, so its acceleration is $a_{\text{ground}} = g$ downwards.

2. For an observer inside the lift (non-inertial frame accelerating downward with acceleration $a$):
$$a_{\text{lift}} = g - a \quad (\text{downwards})$$

3. The ratio of the acceleration observed inside the lift to that on the ground is:
$$\frac{a_{\text{lift}}}{a_{\text{ground}}} = \frac{g - a}{g}$$
Hence, the ratio is $(g - a) : g$.

question_text: A particle moves with a velocity $v = \alpha t^2$ along a straight line. The average speed in time interval $t = 0$ to $t = T$ is
solution:
Average speed is given by the total distance covered divided by total time:
$$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\int_0^T v\, dt}{\int_0^T dt}$$

Evaluating the numerator:
$$\int_0^T \alpha t^2\, dt = \left[ \frac{\alpha t^3}{3} \right]_0^T = \frac{\alpha T^3}{3}$$

Dividing by total time $T$:
$$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\frac{\alpha T^3}{3}}{T} = \frac{\alpha T^2}{3}$$

question_text:
The position ($x$) of a particle on a straight-line motion is given by $x = 2 + 10t - 5t^2\text{ (m)}$. Its velocity ($v$) is best represented by

[Refer to the given $v\text{--}t$ graph options]
diagram_description: Option (1) shows a straight line starting at $v = 10\text{ m/s}$ at $t = 0$ and decreasing linearly to $v = 0$ at $t = 1\text{ s}$. Option (2) starts at $v = 20\text{ m/s}$ and decreases linearly to $0$ at $t = 1\text{ s}$. Options (3) and (4) show non-linear curves.
solution:
Given position equation:
$$x = 2 + 10t - 5t^2$$
Velocity is the derivative of position with respect to time:
$$v = \frac{dx}{dt} = 10 - 10t$$

This is the equation of a straight line $v = -10t + 10$ with:
- Intercept on $v$-axis (at $t = 0$): $v = 10\text{ m/s}$
- Intercept on $t$-axis (when $v = 0$): $10 - 10t = 0 \implies t = 1\text{ s}$
- Slope: $-10\text{ m/s}^2$ (constant negative acceleration)

Graph (1) correctly shows a straight line starting from $v = 10\text{ m/s}$ at $t = 0$ and reaching $0$ at $t = 1\text{ s}$.

question_text: A car travels $A$ to $B$ with speed $V_1$ and returns to $A$ with speed $V_2$, the average speed of the car $V$ is
solution:
Let distance from $A$ to $B$ be $d$.
Total distance covered for round trip is $2d$.

Time taken to travel from $A$ to $B$:
$$t_1 = \frac{d}{V_1}$$
Time taken to return from $B$ to $A$:
$$t_2 = \frac{d}{V_2}$$

Total time taken:
$$t = t_1 + t_2 = \frac{d}{V_1} + \frac{d}{V_2} = d\left(\frac{V_1 + V_2}{V_1 V_2}\right)$$

Average speed:
$$V_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\text{Total Distance}}{\text{Total Time}} = \frac{2d}{d\left(\frac{V_1 + V_2}{V_1 V_2}\right)} = \frac{2V_1 V_2}{V_1 + V_2}$$
Note: While average velocity is zero, average speed is non-zero and equals $\frac{2V_1 V_2}{V_1 + V_2}$.

question_text: A boy fallen freely from a building of height $320\text{ m}$. After $5\text{ second}$ superman jumps downward with initial speed $u$. Such that the boy can be saved. The minimum value of $u$ is (assume $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
solution:
1. Time taken by the falling boy to reach the ground ($h = 320\text{ m}$, $u_0 = 0$):
$$h = \frac{1}{2}gt_1^2 \implies 320 = \frac{1}{2}(10)t_1^2 = 5t_1^2$$
$$t_1^2 = 64 \implies t_1 = 8\text{ s}$$

2. Superman jumps $5\text{ s}$ later, so the maximum time Superman has to catch the boy before hitting ground is:
$$t_2 = 8 - 5 = 3\text{ s}$$

3. In this time interval $t_2 = 3\text{ s}$, Superman must cover the same distance $320\text{ m}$:
$$h = ut_2 + \frac{1}{2}gt_2^2$$
$$320 = u(3) + \frac{1}{2}(10)(3)^2 = 3u + 45$$
$$3u = 320 - 45 = 275 \implies u = \frac{275}{3} \approx 91.67\text{ m/s}$$

Rounding off gives $91.6\text{ m/s}$.

question_text: The displacement $x$ of a body having relation with time as $x = 3t^2 - 6t + 7$, then distance covered by body in first two seconds is [where $x$ is in metre and $t$ is in second]
solution:
Velocity of the body is given by:
$$v = \frac{dx}{dt} = 6t - 6$$

The particle changes its direction of motion when $v = 0$:
$$6t - 6 = 0 \implies t = 1\text{ s}$$
Since $t = 1\text{ s}$ falls within the interval $[0, 2\text{ s}]$, distance must be computed separately for each segment of monotonic motion:

1. At $t = 0\text{ s}$: $x(0) = 3(0)^2 - 6(0) + 7 = 7\text{ m}$
2. At $t = 1\text{ s}$: $x(1) = 3(1)^2 - 6(1) + 7 = 4\text{ m}$
   Distance in first second: $|x(1) - x(0)| = |4 - 7| = 3\text{ m}$

3. At $t = 2\text{ s}$: $x(2) = 3(2)^2 - 6(2) + 7 = 12 - 12 + 7 = 7\text{ m}$
   Distance in second second: $|x(2) - x(1)| = |7 - 4| = 3\text{ m}$

Total distance covered in first 2 seconds:
$$d = 3\text{ m} + 3\text{ m} = 6\text{ m}$$
